Let

\[
F(x)=\lfloor 2x\rfloor+\lfloor 4x\rfloor+\lfloor 6x\rfloor+\lfloor 8x\rfloor.
\]

Set \(y=2x\). Since \(x\) ranges over all real numbers, so does \(y\), and

\[
F(x)=\lfloor y\rfloor+\lfloor 2y\rfloor+\lfloor 3y\rfloor+\lfloor 4y\rfloor.
\]

Write \(y=n+r\), where \(n\in\mathbb Z\) and \(0\le r<1\). Then

\[
\begin{aligned}
F(x)
&=(n+\lfloor r\rfloor)+(2n+\lfloor 2r\rfloor)\\
&\quad +(3n+\lfloor 3r\rfloor)+(4n+\lfloor 4r\rfloor)\\
&=10n+\left(\lfloor r\rfloor+\lfloor 2r\rfloor+\lfloor 3r\rfloor+\lfloor 4r\rfloor\right).
\end{aligned}
\]

Since \(0\le r<1\), \(\lfloor r\rfloor=0\). Now determine the possible values of

\[
H(r)=\lfloor 2r\rfloor+\lfloor 3r\rfloor+\lfloor 4r\rfloor.
\]

The only points in \([0,1)\) where \(H(r)\) can change are

\[
r=\frac14,\frac13,\frac12,\frac23,\frac34.
\]

Evaluating on the resulting intervals gives:

\[
\begin{array}{c|c}
r\text{ interval} & H(r)\\
\hline
[0,\frac14) & 0\\[2mm]
[\frac14,\frac13) & 1\\[2mm]
[\frac13,\frac12) & 2\\[2mm]
[\frac12,\frac23) & 4\\[2mm]
[\frac23,\frac34) & 5\\[2mm]
[\frac34,1) & 6
\end{array}
\]

Thus the expression can only produce numbers congruent to

\[
0,1,2,4,5,6 \pmod{10}.
\]

Conversely, each of these six residues is actually attainable by choosing \(r=0,\frac14,\frac13,\frac12,\frac23,\frac34\), respectively.

Among the integers \(1,2,\dots,1000\), each residue class modulo \(10\) occurs exactly \(100\) times. Since \(6\) residue classes are attainable, the number of expressible integers is

\[
6\cdot 100=600.
\]

\[
\boxed{600}
\]
